info.title: weebo-notify
info.description: Rich, multi-channel, multi-device notification platform. Notifications are lifecycle objects: they carry state, accumulate revisions, expose actions and collect receipts.

oneOf.description: One option of the `choice` action registered under `key`.

InteractionId.description: One recorded interaction: an acknowledgement, a reply, a pick (design §2.3).

Membership.description: The scopes one principal holds in one channel.

principal.description: Who; users and service accounts are members alike (§5.2bis).

scopes.description: What they may do; never empty.

allOf.description: The key's metadata, exactly as `GET /apikeys` will show it from now on.

secret.description: `wnk_<prefix>_<secret>`. Store it now; no endpoint can show it again.

MintedKey.description: A newly minted key: the only response that ever carries its secret (T12).

expires_at.description: When it expires — 15 minutes at most (design §5.3).

token.description: The token itself, Ed25519-signed by us.

Notification.description: A notification and its current state.

closed_at.description: When it last closed, starting its retention clock; `None` while live (§7.2bis).

deleted_at.description: Set on deletion; the row survives long enough to broadcast a tombstone (§7.2bis).

oneOf.description: The publisher's own identifier, when it upserted by one (§2.2).

head.description: The highest-`seq` revision applied so far — the current truth.

last_seq.description: Highest `seq` assigned. The next revision gets `last_seq + 1`.

revision_count.description: How many revisions have been recorded (equals `last_seq` unless rehydrated partially).

ttl.description: Retention as resolved by the channel policy.

NotificationId.description: A notification, stable across every revision it accumulates (design §2.2).

NotificationKind.description: Which of the two publishing shapes produced this notification (§2.2).

NtfyBody.description: An ntfy JSON publish, sent to the ntfy root.

click.description: A link, published as a `view` action.

NtfyMessage.description: What ntfy answers to a publish.

time.description: Unix seconds when the server received it.

topic.description: The channel it was published into.

Origin.description: Where an object came from, and therefore who may change it.

items.description: The rows, in the ordering of the endpoint.

PreferenceEvent.description: This user's whole delivery preference state, DND and silences together (§7.4, §8.1).

silences.description: Every silence currently in force for them.

PresignBody.description: What a client asks to upload.

channel.description: Where the publisher intends to publish it; requires `publish` there (design §6.1).

content_length.description: The declared size, checked against §8.2's ceiling **before** signing.

content_type.description: The declared media type, imposed in the signature.

expires_at.description: When the signature stops working (short-lived: it is a bearer credential).

headers.description: Headers the client must send verbatim; they are covered by the signature.

id.description: The id to reference in a payload once the upload succeeds.

oneOf.description: A human, whether they arrived with an OIDC token or with a personal API key.
A bot with a name of its own.
A key attached to a channel and to nobody else; use a service account when attribution matters (§5.2).

channel.description: The channel that owns the key.

key.description: The key itself. Never the secret.

oneOf.description: A CI job, identified by the claims of the token it exchanged (design §5.3).

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer that vouched for the job.

Principal.description: The identity behind a request, after authentication.

Priority.description: How loudly a notification asks for attention (§2.2); `Urgent` only bypasses DND if the recipient opted in (§7.4).

Problem.description: The `application/problem+json` body every refusal carries; clients match on `code`.

code.description: The stable code to match on; absent only for server-side failures.

retry_after_seconds.description: When to come back, on a `429`. Mirrors the `Retry-After` header.

status.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body as RFC 9457 asks.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary. Prose, and subject to change.

Profile.description: Everything a client shows about a person, beyond their identity.

oneOf.description:
The object holding their uploaded picture (§2.4). Never synced from OIDC
`picture`: fetching token-supplied URLs would be an SSRF primitive.

display_name.description: What clients show. Falls back to the identity when unset.

overridden.description: The fields this person set themselves, rather than following the identity provider.

timezone.description: An IANA timezone name such as `Europe/Paris`, validated against the real database.

ProfileBody.description:
A partial edit of the caller's profile: an absent field is left alone, `null` hands it
back to the identity provider, a value claims it against later logins (§2.4).

display_name.description: The name shown next to everything this person publishes.

timezone.description: An IANA name such as `Europe/Paris`; the default timezone for quiet hours (§7.4).

ProfileField.description: A field of a profile that can be claimed by its owner.

Progress.description: How far along a long-running thing is, in the publisher's own units.

allOf.description: The content itself, flattened into the same JSON object.

oneOf.description: Priority.
Lifecycle position; present at creation makes it a lifecycle notification (§2.2).
Status.
Retention, resolved against the channel policy (§7.2bis).

allOf.description:
A revision as a publisher submits it; absent fields keep the head's value on
update and take channel defaults on creation.
The revision itself, flattened into the same object.

PublishBody.description: `POST /notifications`: the upsert body's revision draft plus its channel (§8.3).

Published.description: What a publish produced; also the stored idempotency response, replayed verbatim.

cursor.description: Where it landed in the event log.

notification.description: The notification as it now stands.

replayed.description: Whether this is a replay of an earlier identical request.

retention.description: What the channel policy did to the requested retention, so a clamp is visible.

revision.description: The revision that was just recorded.

oneOf.description: None: reachable only while it holds a stream (CLI, TUI, service account).
Web Push (RFC 8030/8291), for browsers and installed PWAs; the browser holds the keys (§6.2).

auth.description: The subscription's `auth` secret, as given by the browser.

endpoint.description: The push service endpoint the browser handed us.

p256dh.description: The subscription's `p256dh` key, as given by the browser.

oneOf.description: UnifiedPush, self-hosted end to end (§7.1bis).

endpoint.description: The distributor endpoint to POST to.

oneOf.description: APNs — the one part of the stack that cannot be self-hosted (design §15).

PushTransport.description: How the server reaches a device when its client is not connected.

QuietHours.description: One recurring weekly window of quiet (design §7.4).

days.description:
The days it applies to (**empty means every day**). A window crossing midnight
belongs to the day it starts on.

end.description: When it ends; earlier than `start` means the window crosses midnight.

start.description: When quiet begins, on the local clock.

timezone.description: The IANA zone `start` and `end` are read in (the preference's, not the device's).

Readership.description: The "seen by 3/5" readership: who saw it and when, plus a delivered-device count (§7.3, §10.3).

audience.description: How many people could see it, or `None` when access is group-derived (show "seen by 3").

seen.description: Who saw it, oldest sighting first — reading order, like the timeline.

Readiness.description: Readiness answer: the overall verdict plus per-dependency detail.

checks.description: One entry per dependency actually configured on this replica.

ready.description: `true` only when every checked dependency is reachable.

oneOf.description: Which device; absent for a service account's logical subscription (§5.2bis).

principal.description: Who. Only ever a principal's own devices.

oneOf.description: Which device saw it, when the client is one.

Reconciliation.description: What the last GitOps pass did (design §11, §10.4bis).

at.description: When this replica last applied the configuration.

pending.description:
Bindings by `oidc_sub` or `email` naming somebody who has never logged in, which
grant nothing until that person's first login (§14.1).

removed.description: Channels that left the configuration and were archived or deleted.

trigger.description: What caused this pass — boot, the timer, or `SIGHUP` (§11).

RecordedInteraction.description: What recording an interaction did: whether anything changed worth broadcasting.

oneOf.description: The interaction that now stands; absent on `unchanged`.

Revision.description: One immutable step of a notification's life.

received_at.description: When the server received it — the server's clock, not the publisher's.

seq.description: Server-assigned, monotonic within the notification, starting at 1; the last-write-wins arbiter.

state.description: Lifecycle position as of this revision.

allOf.description: The content itself, flattened into the same JSON object.

oneOf.description: Priority.
Lifecycle position; present at creation makes it a lifecycle notification (§2.2).
Status.
Retention, resolved against the channel policy (§7.2bis).

RevisionDraft.description:
A revision as a publisher submits it; absent fields keep the head's value on
update and take channel defaults on creation.

RevisionEvent.description: A revision, denormalised so a reconnecting client can render it from one event (§8.1).

created_at.description: When the notification was first created.

oneOf.description: The publisher's own identifier, when it upserted by one.

payload.description: The content, in the clear (TLS stream; sealing only applies to push, §6.2).

seq.description: Server-assigned sequence within the notification, the last-write-wins arbiter (§2.2).

state.description: Lifecycle position as of this revision.

RevisionId.description: One immutable revision of a notification.

Scope.description: What a principal may do in a channel (design §5.2).

ServiceAccount.description: A named machine identity (§5.2bis), the recommended owner for anything durable.

oneOf.description: Who created it through the API (and may deactivate it); `None` for managed accounts.

disabled_at.description: Set on deactivation, which revokes its keys and cuts its streams immediately (§8, T25).

display_name.description: What clients show — "published by ArgoCD", not by an opaque id.

id.description: Its name, and the id used everywhere it appears.

ServiceAccountId.description: A service account, named so a timeline can say who published (§5.2bis).

Sighting.description: One person and when they first saw the notification (§7.3, §10.3).

at.description: When they first saw it, across all their devices.

author.description: Who, with a display name where the reader is entitled to it (§2.4).

Silence.description: An active silence, held per user.

until.description: When it lifts; `None` only for a notification-scoped silence, which ends with the notification.

user.description: Whose it is. Silences never leak across users (scenario T20).

oneOf.description: How long, e.g. `2h`. A group-scoped silence must say.

scope.description: How far it reaches. Defaults to this notification alone.

oneOf.description: One notification.
Everything sharing a `group_key` (design §2.3).

SinkId.description: Which sink of which channel, written as `kind:destination` (never contains secrets).

State.description: Where a notification is in its lifecycle.

Status.description: What the notification is saying, orthogonally to where it is in its lifecycle.

SyncPage.description:
A catch-up page: events plus the per-user expired counts (§7.2bis), the
compaction count (§7.2) and DND-deferred ids (§7.4).

compacted.description:
How many revisions the compaction folded away, over the whole window since
`after` and not just this page — so the first page of a catch-up carries the
total, and that is the one a client reads it from.

Counted over at most the first ten thousand events of the window (in no
particular order): past that it is a **lower bound**, "at least this many",
rather than a count that could cost a long absence its catch-up.

deferred_by_dnd.description:
Notifications on this page delayed on purpose by a quiet period (§7.4); kept
off the events because events are identical for every reader.

expired.description: Per channel, how many notifications expired unseen during the absence.

oneOf.description: Pass back as `after` for the next page. `None` means fully caught up.

TombstoneReason.description: Why a notification stopped existing, as broadcast in a `tombstone` event (§8.1).

Trigger.description: What made a reconciliation pass happen (design §11, §10.4bis).

TrustPolicyCard.description: One trust policy as the console shows it.

channel_scoped.description: Whether it came from a channel's own `publishers` block, which wins over a global one (§11).

Ttl.description: How long to keep it: a single-unit duration such as `48h`, or `0` for forever.

TtlPolicy.description: What retention a channel allows (§7.2bis, configured per channel in §11).

allow_forever.description: Whether `"0"` (keep forever) is accepted; off by default.

default.description: Applied when the publisher says nothing.

oneOf.description: Forced ceiling. A longer request is clamped down to it.

TtlResolution.description: The outcome of applying a [`TtlPolicy`] to a request.

oneOf.description: Set when the request exceeded the channel ceiling, so the clamp is visible (T6).

UnreadCount.description: What one channel's unread badge shows (design §7.3, §10.4).

channel.description: The channel the badge hangs off.

unread.description:
How many of its notifications this principal has not read; never zero (such
channels are omitted).

UserCard.description: A person, as the member picker shows them.

email.description: Their email, when the identity provider released one.

UserId.description: A human, created on first OIDC login.

WallClock.description: A time of day on a wall clock, to the minute, rendered `HH:MM`.

WebPushKey.description: The identity of this server, as a push service knows it.

application_server_key.description: The uncompressed P-256 public point, base64url: `applicationServerKey` (RFC 8292).

Whoami.description: The caller's own id, to name itself as `owner` of e.g. a personal API key (§5.2).

bearer.description: An OIDC access token, or an API key of the form `wnk_<prefix>_<secret>`.
